slot.brief: Given a function built with the greatest integer function, invert (or restrict) to determine which values are excluded from its range.

stem: Let $[t]$ denote the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. The set of all real numbers that do not belong to the range of the function $f(x) = \dfrac{x + [x]}{x - [x]}$, defined on $\mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{Z}$, is

verdicts.working: Write x = n + t, n∈ℤ, t∈(0,1). Then f = (2n+t)/t = 1 + 2n/t. For n=0, f=1 exactly. For n≥1, f∈(2n+1,∞), union (3,∞). For n≤-1, f∈(-∞,1-2|n|), union (-∞,-1). Range = (-∞,-1)∪{1}∪(3,∞); numerics confirm only value in [-1,3] attained is 1. Complement = [-1,1)∪(1,3].

working:
For any $x \in \mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{Z}$, write $x = [x] + \{x\}$, where $[x] \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $\{x\} \in (0, 1)$.

The function can be rewritten as:
$$f(x) = \dfrac{[x] + \{x\} + [x]}{\{x\}} = \dfrac{2[x] + \{x\}}{\{x\}} = 1 + \dfrac{2[x]}{\{x\}}$$

Let $y = f(x)$. We analyze the possible values of $y$ by cases of $[x]$:
1. If $[x] = 0$, then $x \in (0, 1)$, so $f(x) = 1 + 0 = 1$. Thus, $1$ is in the range.
2. If $[x] = n \ge 1$, since $0 < \{x\} < 1$, we have $\dfrac{1}{\{x\}} \in (1, \infty)$, so:
$$y = 1 + \dfrac{2n}{\{x\}} \in (2n + 1, \infty)$$
Taking the union over all $n \ge 1$ gives $(3, \infty)$.
3. If $[x] = -k \le -1$ where $k \ge 1$ is an integer, then:
$$y = 1 - \dfrac{2k}{\{x\}} \in (-\infty, 1 - 2k)$$
Taking the union over all $k \ge 1$ gives $(-\infty, -1)$.

Therefore, the range of $f$ is:
$$\text{Range}(f) = (-\infty, -1) \cup \{1\} \cup (3, \infty)$$

The set of values excluded from the range is the complement in $\mathbb{R}$:
$$\mathbb{R} \setminus \text{Range}(f) = [-1, 1) \cup (1, 3]$$
